# Statistics and Experimentation

Explain the question and assumptions before selecting a formula or test.
Separate descriptive results, uncertainty, statistical significance, practical
importance, and causal conclusions.

## Foundation

- Population, sample, sampling, and sources of bias.
- Mean, median, mode, variance, standard deviation, percentiles, and quartiles.
- Probability, events, conditional probability, and independence.

## Intermediate

- Normal, binomial, and Poisson distributions.
- Sampling distributions and the Central Limit Theorem.
- Confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, p-values, and Type I/II errors.
- Z-tests, t-tests, chi-square tests, and ANOVA.
- Correlation, covariance, and simple regression.

## Advanced

- Logistic and multiple regression.
- A/B testing, experimental design, and statistical power.
- Multiple comparisons and non-parametric tests.
- Regression diagnostics and model assumptions.

## Expert applications

- Bayesian reasoning and inference.
- Causal inference and identification assumptions.
- Time-series analysis.
- Communicating uncertainty and avoiding overclaiming.

## Assessment checks

- Ask learners to interpret results in context, not merely calculate a p-value.
- Check assumptions, sample design, effect size, and limitations.
- Use small, clearly labeled synthetic examples when no data is supplied.
